vignette: Case Vignette for Michael Michael is a 25-year-old African American journalist who has been struggling with significant symptoms following a traumatic event involving police violence. This incident occurred about six months ago when he was covering a protest in his city. The trauma was particularly potent because it involved witnessing the unjust shooting of a fellow protester, whom he had come to know through his reporting. On that fateful day, Michael was capturing footage with his camera when shots rang out unexpectedly. He vividly remembers the sound of gunshots and the screams of the crowd as they scattered for cover. The image of his friend being struck down and bleeding on the ground remains seared into his memory. Since then, he has found himself hyper-vigilant and often looking over his shoulder to check if someone is following him. Michael's daily life is now punctuated by moments where footsteps behind or nearby send waves of panic through him. Michael's occupation as a journalist places him in the public eye frequently, which makes certain triggers particularly potent. He avoids reporting from locations he deems unfamiliar because he feels unable to assess potential dangers accurately. This has led him to decline several assignments that would require him to venture into new neighborhoods or events with large crowds. The fear of being overwhelmed by his memories and emotions is a constant companion. In an effort to cope, Michael often wears concealing clothing to avoid drawing attention to himself. He has also stopped attending certain gatherings where music from the protest might be played, as those songs are now potent triggers that bring back fragments of the trauma he experienced. These avoidance strategies have led to him feeling increasingly isolated, both at work and in his personal life. Michael's girlfriend has noticed a significant change in him since the incident. He often seems distant and preoccupied, making it difficult for them to connect on a deeper level. What frightens Michael most is that these changes might mean he will never be able to do what defined him as a journalist-covering important stories with passion and courage. The memories of that day are vivid and feel more real than his other recollections. He often hears the gunshots in his head and struggles to put them into coherent words when trying to recount the event to others. The inability to articulate these experiences clearly has left him feeling isolated, as if no one truly understands what he went through. Michael's sense of self has been profoundly altered by this trauma. He feels that his life has been irrevocably damaged and that he is no longer capable of the vibrant, engaged person he used to be. His once-thriving career and personal relationships have begun to suffer as a result of these pervasive feelings. He finds it hard to concentrate on work, leading to missed deadlines and a sense of failure. What finally pushed Michael to seek help was an incident where he was covering another protest and the sound of footsteps behind him triggered such intense anxiety that he had to leave the scene abruptly. This realization that his condition is worsening has made him desperate for support. He hopes therapy can provide strategies to manage his symptoms, allowing him to reclaim some sense of normalcy in his life. Michael's journey so far has been marked by a profound loss of happiness and an overwhelming feeling of being trapped in a cycle of fear and avoidance. His current state reflects not just the trauma itself but also its enduring impact on his daily functioning and relationships. The road ahead is uncertain, but Michael is determined to reclaim some measure of control over his life.
